_comment: PEMF -- the in-game guide. Opened with H while sailing (keys.ini).
Each topic is a menu; each entry closes on a card explaining it.

menus.title: PEMF -- what this mod adds to your voyages. Choose a topic.

options.outcome: You cannot fly colours you do not have. When a governor grants you a letter of marque, his crown's flag comes with it, and it is yours for good. You always have your own colours and the black flag.
Press Q while sailing to choose which flag to fly from the ones in your locker. The one flying is marked. (The key can be changed in PEMF\keys.ini.)
The trader at the back of a tavern sometimes has a crown's flag as well as his usual wares. It costs gold, and it lets you fly colours no governor gave you.

There is no crown to choose at the tavern: a new career begins in a pirate haven, serving no one and flying the black flag. Sail where you like and talk to any governor -- his letter of marque is what ties you to a crown.

menus.title: Suspicion -- how far they have seen through you.

options.outcome: It depends on how a crown regards you. The black flag makes every crown suspicious. Their own colours with their letter of marque make you a friend; without one it is a disguise. An enemy's colours only bother them if they already think badly of you. It rises slowly -- faster the closer they get and the less they like you. The panel at the top right shows it.

Attacking, taking or sacking what belongs to a crown is what turns suspicion into certainty: their meter jumps at once, more the worse the deed, and it costs you their good opinion -- even a crown that commissioned you. Do it while wearing someone's colours and the disguise is blown.
At the top of the meter, the nearest ship of that crown falls in astern and shadows you. Nothing is lost yet. Keep your guns quiet for a minute or two and she falls away, and the meter drops back.

Near the top, a ship comes about and asks who you are. Hold the ruse (a gamble, better with a discreet officer), strike the false colours (no harm done), or run for it (out of sight, suspicion cools fast).
Sail where nobody of theirs can see you and it falls. It falls faster once you are well away from the water where it was raised.

menus.title: The crowns, their opinion of you, and their hunters.

options.outcome: Each crown thinks something of you. Below zero they are your enemy: their ports are closed to you, and their governor, merchant and shipwright will not deal with you. The tavern still serves anyone.
A crown you are below zero with sends pirate-hunters, one at a time. How many depends on how badly they think of you and on what you have actually done to them. A hunter chases you wherever you sail.
Outrun her, outlast her (she gives up after a few minutes), or put into port and stay -- she will not wait outside the harbour for ever. Each escape buys time before that crown sends another.

Most of what being caught out costs is forgiven in time if nothing more comes of it. A harbourmaster's palm, greased on the waterfront, makes a port's crown forget sooner. What you actually did is remembered.

Walk the waterfront from the town menu: bribe the harbourmaster, listen to the gossip (who is hunting you, whose ports are shut), stand the dockhands a round for a few new hands, or lay in fresh stores.

Manage yer crew! in the town menu finds officers to sign on -- a quartermaster, a sailing master, a surgeon and others. Each brings talents (and sometimes flaws), and some things only happen with the right officer aboard.
Prices move. Word comes in of shortages and gluts around particular ports, and a town at war pays more for food and cannon.
While sailing (not in battle or in port): Q chooses your colours, C opens your crew and officers, H opens this guide. All three can be changed in PEMF\keys.ini.

The wind wanders slowly about the trades, and now and then a front swings it hard. Storms make up to windward and drift with it; inside one you are driven along, and in its heart your ships take damage.

Battles are louder and messier: wreckage and men go into the sea with every hit, the guns smoke harder, smoke hangs where shot strikes, and your broadsides shake the deck. PEMF\combat.ini tunes all of it.
Wreckage, castaways, fever, deserters, a fair wind -- events come along as you sail, and some depend on who you have aboard.
